findings.title: The demo's AWS-call count is tautological, and design §4.3 asked for enforcement
findings.detail: main() calls _count_aws_calls() AFTER all three legs have completed. That function creates attempted = {'count': 0}, registers the before-send hooks on the two client event systems, and returns attempted['count'] in the same call, so the value is 0 by construction and no leg call could ever have been refused. Consequences: the rendered line 'AWS API calls attempted = 0' states nothing about the run, the following line 'a before-send hook would fail the run' is false for the run just printed, and the guard 'return 1 if mismatches or aws_calls else 0' has a dead second clause. The hook targets do resolve (middleware.cognito.meta.events and rate_limit.dynamodb.meta.client.meta.events both resolve to an EventAliaser, measured after main(['--json']) returned 0), so the mechanism works and is merely installed at the wrong moment. Design revision 8 §4.3 is explicit: 'A call that would leave the process fails the demo rather than being tallied afterwards', so this is a deviation, not a judgement call. findings.md and verification.md both repeat the enforcement claim, in the one artifact the retirement gate depends on.
findings.action: Install the before-send hooks inside _install_containment() before leg 1, hold the counter where both functions can read it, and reduce _count_aws_calls() to a read. Then correct the enforcement wording in findings.md and verification.md §10 if needed.

findings.title: urllib.request.urlopen is replaced globally and never restored
findings.detail: _install_containment() assigns urllib.request.urlopen = transport directly and nothing puts the original back. The demo fixture in tests/test_demo_coupon_giftcard_sample.py wraps wix_ecom._key_cache and sys.modules['boto3'] in monkeypatch.setitem (so those are restored) but never touches urlopen. Confirmed by inspection after an in-process run: urllib.request.urlopen is still a WixTransport once main() returns, with a drained queue, so any later call raises UnexpectedWixCall, which is a BaseException and escapes every except Exception in the tree. Nine other test modules reference urlopen and all sort after test_demo_* alphabetically; they pass only because each patches urlopen itself. A test that calls urlopen without its own patch would fail naming the wrong module, and a test asserting 'no network call happens' could pass because the stub refused rather than because the code abstained.
findings.action: Save the original in _install_containment() and restore it in main() (try/finally), or move the urlopen patch into the test fixture so monkeypatch owns the teardown.

findings.title: The registered botocore before-send hooks outlive the test session
findings.detail: The refuse handler is registered on module-level, session-lifetime clients (lambda_utils.middleware.cognito, lambda_utils.rate_limit.dynamodb) and is never unregistered; main() is invoked five times across the demo test file, so handlers accumulate. Any later test that exercises those clients for real would get an uncatchable UnexpectedAwsCall. Latent today only because test_rate_limit.py replaces lambda_utils.rate_limit.dynamodb wholesale with a MagicMock, bypassing the hooked client.
findings.action: Unregister the handler on the way out (botocore unregister), or register it inside a scope the caller controls, so a pytest session is not left with permanent raising hooks on shared clients.

findings.title: The printed idempotency key discloses the demo code, so the 'no clear bearer-value code' claim is stronger than the fact
findings.detail: demo_code(reference_id) is 'WDGC' + sha256(reference_id).hexdigest()[:16] upper-cased and idempotency_key(reference_id) is 'wd-gc-' + the same digest. The demo masks the code everywhere and prints the idempotency key in full, so the masked code is recoverable by stripping decoration and upper-casing. This is documented in the demo_code docstring and asserted positively by the suite (assert demo in key). Production is unaffected because card_code is HMAC-keyed and the same test asserts keyed not in key and key not in keyed. verification.md §10's grep-based conclusion 'no clear bearer-value code' is literally true of the string and not of the information.
findings.action: Mask the printed idempotency key, or state the reconstructability at the point where the zero-occurrence grep result is reported.

findings.title: Fetch count disagrees between findings.md and the contract transcript
findings.detail: findings.md says 'Six fetches of the live dev.wix.com markdown rendition'; docs/execution/wix-contract-verification-20261002.md tabulates five (1, 2, 2b, 3, 4) and states 'Five pages, five HTTP 200 lines', and the commit message says five curl GETs.
findings.action: Correct the count in findings.md to match the transcript.

findings.title: credit() lost its once_key idempotency with no statement of where idempotency must live
findings.detail: credit() is now a plain addition and has no production caller anywhere under amplify/, which is what makes the removal safe today. The docstring argues correctly that a genuine top-up must not be idempotent, but a future top-up route inherits a non-idempotent money function with no pointer to where the guard belongs. Separately, one test name still reads test_the_claim_row_is_settled_by_the_decrement_... for a path that no longer has a _decrement.
findings.action: Add a line to credit()'s docstring naming where a top-up caller must provide idempotency, and rename the stale test.
